::: {#sol-mean-pixel}

```{python}
#| code-fold: show
import textwrap

print(images.dtype)
try:
    images[0].mean()
except RuntimeError as err:
    print(textwrap.fill(str(err), 60))
first_mean = images[0].float().mean().item()
print(images[0].float().dtype, first_mean)
```

The pixels were read as whole numbers, so the [tensor](#def-tensor) stores 64-bit integers,
`torch.int64`, which PyTorch also calls `Long`.
`.mean()` refuses them, since an average of integers is not in general an integer.
Converting the tensor with `.float()` to 32-bit floating-point numbers fixes it:
the first image's average pixel is `r sprintf("%.2f", py$first_mean)`, on the file's scale of 0 to 16.

:::
